title: Access Quick Actions — Command Bar prototype notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures a focused prototype for an "Access Quick Actions" command bar inside the Org/Team settings surface. Goal: give admins and power users a fast, discoverable way to perform small-but-frequent access tasks without navigating deep settings pages. This is intentionally small-scope — not a full RBAC editor — but a complement to the existing access pages.

High-level UX hypothesis:
- Many users perform small, repeated tasks (create API key, rotate service account key, run an audit query, grant a temporary role) and the current flow requires 3–6 clicks.
- Exposing a keyboard-first command bar (Cmd/Ctrl+K) and a compact button in the org header will reduce task time and surface discoverability for advanced workflows.
- The command bar should be permission-aware: only show actions the user can complete and provide inline escalation/justification flows when applicable.

Primary user goals to validate:
- Create a short-lived API key for a service quickly.
- Rotate an existing key with minimal context switching.
- Jump to the most recent audit entries for a given user or service account.
- Grant/revoke a well-known role to a user or service account for a bounded duration (one-off).

Key components and behaviors:
1) Invocation
- Keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the bar centered on the screen.
- UI affordance: a compact pill in the top-right org header with a lightning icon that opens the bar on click.
- Mobile: accessible via a condensed toolbar item in the org menu (opens full-screen modal).

2) Query language and suggestions
- Free-text with incremental suggestions. Examples: "create key for svc-billing", "rotate key api-123", "audit user:melinda", "grant role:viewer to jason for 4h".
- Fuzzy match on resources (org/team/service-account names) and actions.
- Show an action/result preview line below suggestion: e.g., "Create API key — svc-billing — short-lived (7d)".
- Support natural modifiers: duration (for), expiry date (until), scope (team:analytics).

3) Permission gating and inline justification
- If user lacks permission, inline CTA shows required permission and an optional "Request temporary approval" flow that opens a pre-filled approval request to admins (includes reason text and TTL).
- For role grants that require audit metadata, require a justification string before completion.

4) Confirmation and ephemeral tokens
- For key creation/rotation, show one-time token copy screen with explicit copy CTA and a reminder to store the token. Provide a short countdown / visibility timer for security note.

Low-fidelity wireframe (ASCII):

+------------------------------------------------------------+
| Org header                             [Search] [Lightning⚡] |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
|                       Command Bar (centered modal)         |
|  --------------------------------------------------------  |
|  > create key for svc-billing  -- suggestions dropdown    |
|  --------------------------------------------------------  |
|  Action preview: Create API key · Short-lived (7d) · team:billing |
|  [Confirm]  [Cancel]                                       |
+------------------------------------------------------------+

Microinteractions and accessibility:
- Keyboard nav through suggestions (up/down), Enter to accept, Esc to close.
- Screen reader announcements for action preview and permission requirements.
- Color contrast and focus states must meet AA.
- Provide a persistent way to access command history for the current user (keyboard: Cmd+K then Up to cycle past commands).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Command bar launches via keyboard and header CTA.
- Users can create a short-lived API key for a service account and view the token copy screen.
- Users can run an audit quick search (user or service account) and see the top 25 most recent entries inline with a "open in audit view" link.
- Permission gating shows clear messaging and optional request-for-approval flow.

Rollout plan and telemetry:
- Phased beta: 1) internal alpha for SE/solutions-eng, 2) opt-in beta for paid orgs, 3) default-on for org admins.
- Metrics to collect: command invocation rate, conversion (invoke -> complete), avg time-to-complete, error rate (permission rejections), number of approval requests created, and task abandonment.
- Heatmap event: which suggestions are selected.

Edge cases and risk mitigation:
- Long lists of similarly named resources: prioritize recent-used and exact-match; show resource type badges (svc, team, user).
- Sensitive actions (permanent key creation, role:admin grant): require an interstitial with a clear list of consequences and a mandatory justification field.
- Race on rotation: warn if the target key was updated less than N minutes ago.
- Offline/mobile: show offline state and prevent token creation unless connected.

Backlog (initial tickets):
- INF-8812: Command bar core component + keyboard bindings (E2E).
- INF-8813: Suggestion engine: resource indexing and fuzzy match service.
- INF-8814: API: create/rotate key endpoints + one-time token response.
- INF-8815: Audit quick query API + inline result schema.
- INF-8816: Approval request flow + email/Slack notification integration.
- INF-8817: Accessibility pass & screen reader QA.

Open questions to resolve in grooming:
- TTL policy defaults: should short-lived keys default to 7 days or 24 hours for internal orgs?
- Do we allow command macros (save a command string for reuse) in MVP? Pros/cons for security posture.
- How much of the RBAC model do we expose in suggestions (roles vs. permissions)? Simplest is role-level only.
- Should we rate-limit command invocation per user to prevent accidental mass ops?

Design notes for visual/engineering handoff:
- Component-based: CommandBar (shell), SuggestionList (data), ActionPreview (validation + permission), ResultModal (tokens / audit list).
- Keep the shell independent of backend: support a stub suggestion provider for offline demos.
- Use existing token copy component and reuse the audit table for inline results.
- Provide clear error codes from backend to map to UX messages (e.g., 403->permission_hint, 409->conflict_race, 429->rate_limited).

Next steps (short):
- Design: produce 2 variants (compact + expanded) and an accessible spec — due 2025-02-21.
- Engineering: spike INF-8812 and INF-8813 (2-week spike) to estimate integration cost — start 2025-02-24.
- PM: finalize TTL default and approval flow decision by grooming 2025-02-28.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and intended to reduce common friction for power users. Please call out any operational security concerns early (esp. around default TTLs and approval flows).
- Related: map this to the existing role-scoped keys UX work to avoid duplication.
